tasks.instruction: The kettle cools by 3 degrees per tick and must stop as soon as its temperature is at or below room temperature; right now it keeps cooling one tick too long when it lands exactly on room temperature.
tasks.note: Loop stop predicate: the fix picks the strict comparison. The wrong edit swaps the initial state and the extra.

tasks.instruction: Return how many days the stock can fully serve the daily demand (the demand list repeats every four days, at most 12 days), not the stock that is left.
tasks.note: Record state (stock, days); the result must read field 1. The wrong edit also shortens the cap.

tasks.instruction: Halve p0 repeatedly, stopping once it is 1 or less, but halve at most p1 times instead of a fixed 8 times.
tasks.note: Loop count becomes an operand. The wrong edit also loosens the predicate so it halves down to 0.

tasks.instruction: Return the number of minutes of inflow (the list of four inflows repeats, at most 16 minutes) until the level reaches the capacity p0; it currently reports one minute too many.
tasks.note: Start state fix: minutes start at 0. The wrong edit changes the stop predicate instead.

tasks.instruction: Keep snoozing by p1 minutes while the sleeper is not yet awake (awake means the time has reached p0), at most 10 snoozes, and return the time; it currently uses the predicate with the opposite meaning.
tasks.note: State (time, awake); the predicate compares a bool field with eq. The wrong edit uses the right predicate but starts awake.

tasks.instruction: The traffic light has three colours numbered 0, 1, 2 and cycles 0, 1, 2, 0; return how many ticks (at most 5) it takes to go from colour p0 to colour p1.
tasks.note: State machine; the modulus passed to the step is the cycle length 3.

tasks.instruction: Count bounces while the height is at least p2 (each bounce keeps p1 tenths of the height), for at most 30 bounces; it currently uses a fixed floor of 10 and a cap of 20.
tasks.note: Fix both the loop count and the extra passed to the predicate. The wrong edit fixes only the count.

tasks.instruction: Cards 0-12 are clubs, 13-25 diamonds, 26-38 hearts and 39-51 spades; return the suit letter byte from the string, choosing it by dividing the card number by 13.
tasks.note: Index arithmetic into a text table.

tasks.instruction: The door word is OPEN, but the stored string has two letters swapped; fix the string so the check compares against OPEN.
tasks.note: Text fix; the result compares two bools with eq (letter matched vs expected).

tasks.instruction: Return the byte of the word SCHEDULE at position p0 counted from the end, so 0 gives the last letter and 7 the first.
tasks.note: Reverse index; p0 = 8 wraps to 4294967295, which is 7 modulo 8.

tasks.instruction: p0 is an ASCII digit; return the letter on the keyboard row below it, so '1' gives Q, '9' gives O and '0' gives P.
tasks.note: Index arithmetic relies on get taking the index modulo 10; subtracting 49 wraps '0' to index 5.

tasks.instruction: Sum the first p0 bytes of the word INVOICE; the sum must be able to include all seven bytes, but it currently never adds the last one.
tasks.note: Checksum over a string prefix; fold count must equal the text length. Count 8 rereads index 0 for p0 above 7.

tasks.instruction: Scores 0 to 100 map by tens to F (below 60), D, C, B, A; a perfect 100 must also get A, which the current string cannot give.
tasks.note: The text table needs an eleventh entry; dropping an F instead shifts every band.

tasks.instruction: Read one input word and write three times its value (wrapping).
tasks.note: Echo a transformed input; only one word is read.

tasks.instruction: The first input word is the price and the second is the amount paid; write the change, or 0 when the amount paid is less than the price.
tasks.note: Both the comparison and the subtraction must swap operands; the wrong edit swaps only the comparison.

tasks.instruction: Write, with puts, the start hours of three shifts 8 hours apart beginning at hour p1, each wrapped to the 24-hour clock (0 to 23).
tasks.note: puts writes the length 3 first. The wrong edit forgets to wrap the first hour.

tasks.instruction: Read two words and frame each one with the helper, in the order they were read.
tasks.note: The token is passed through an earlier helper twice; order of calls matters.

tasks.instruction: Add the quantity p3 to the count in slot p2 (instead of replacing it) and write the whole count list with puts.
tasks.note: Inventory report with puts; slot index wraps modulo 4.

tasks.instruction: Stamp code 2 for payments of 100 or more and code 1 otherwise, then write the amount.
tasks.note: Token passes through an earlier helper, then a write.

tasks.instruction: Read a low value and then a high value and write with puts the list [high minus low, low, high].
tasks.note: Two reads then puts; the difference wraps when high is below low.

tasks.instruction: Add a helper that divides rounding up (quotient plus one when there is a remainder) and use it so a partly filled box is still counted; each box costs 3.
tasks.note: New helper before the caller. The wrong helper always adds a whole box.

tasks.instruction: Add a helper giving the base fare for an age (under 12: 5, 65 and over: 6, otherwise 10) and use it instead of the flat 10; members (p1) still get 2 off.
tasks.note: Ticketing; boundaries at 12 and 65.

tasks.instruction: Add a helper that averages two values without overflow, as (a and b) plus ((a xor b) shifted right by 1), and use it instead of adding then halving.
tasks.note: Signal smoothing; the start overflows on large inputs.

tasks.instruction: Add a helper that adds one to a given slot of the four counts, and use it to bump slot p1 and then slot p2 (the same slot twice if they are equal).
tasks.note: Array value semantics: the second bump must use the result of the first.

tasks.instruction: Add a helper giving the length in hours of a shift from start to end hour, where an end before the start means the shift runs past midnight, and use it to total two shifts.
tasks.note: Scheduling; a shift whose end equals its start has length 0.

tasks.instruction: p0 is a temperature in Celsius and p1 a threshold in Fahrenheit; add a helper converting Celsius to Fahrenheit (times 9, divided by 5, plus 32) and compare its result with p1 (at least).
tasks.note: Multiplying before dividing keeps precision (37 C is 98 F, not 95).

tasks.instruction: Advance the round number p2 by one when the two votes agree (both yes or both no), not only when both are yes.
tasks.note: Plain bool comparison with eq.

tasks.instruction: Store the new score p1 in slot p2 of the score table only if it beats the score already there; otherwise keep the old score.
tasks.note: Plain get/select/set on a fixed array (game high scores).

tasks.instruction: A withdrawal equal to the balance is allowed; only a withdrawal larger than the balance is refused, and a refused one costs a fee of 5 from the balance.
tasks.note: Account record (balance, refused) built with rec/put and read with at; the fee wraps on tiny balances.

tasks.instruction: Use the fallback value p3 when the two sensor flags disagree, and the reading p2 when they agree.
tasks.note: Plain bool compare with ne (start uses eq).
